guideTitle: 6 Best Motion Sensor Under Cabinet Lights in 2026
metaTitle: Best Motion Under Cabinet Lights in 2026
metaDescription: Six wireless motion sensor under cabinet lights compared by bar length, battery size and light modes for kitchens, pantries and shelves.
introParagraphs: Under cabinet lights solve a very specific problem: the counter is dark because the overhead light throws your own shadow onto the work. A motion sensor version adds a second benefit, since the light comes on as you approach and goes off when you leave, with no switch to find. The differences in this lineup are mostly about bar size and battery. The Gritin 10.2 inch bar packs 84 LEDs, the YLXS set offers five 7.9 inch bars, and the EZVALO 10 inch pair carries a 2400mAh battery in each bar.

We evaluated six wireless bars that fit the angle, comparing LED count, length, battery capacity, light color, modes and how they mount. These are not hard-wired fixtures, so none of them needs an electrician, and all attach with magnets or adhesive. Where a listing gives a figure such as lumens or run time, we use it, and where it does not, we say so rather than guess. Battery size and bar length turned out to matter more than any single feature.
These are convenience lights for ordinary homes. A bar under a cabinet makes a counter easier to use at night, but it is not a safety device and does not replace good general lighting.

products.name: EZVALO 10 Inch Rechargeable Motion Under Cabinet Lights, 2 Pack
products.description:
The EZVALO is the best all-rounder because it spends on the thing that matters most in a wireless bar, which is battery size. Each 10 inch bar carries a 2400mAh rechargeable battery, a bigger cell than the 1100mAh in the YLXS and about the same as the 2000mAh on the Auxoda. A bigger battery means fewer trips to the charging cable.

It offers three modes for different daily needs. Night Motion Mode turns the light on only in the dark when it senses movement, which saves charge during the day, and the other modes give steady or all-hours motion lighting. Brightness is dimmable, so you can set a pantry light low and a counter light higher.

The listing gives no lumen figure or LED count, so we cannot compare brightness with the Gritin's 84 LEDs. Two bars are enough for a single counter run but not a long kitchen. It is the pick for people who want to forget about charging. Charge both bars together so they stay in step.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and pantries where fewer recharges matter most.
cons: Two bars cover one counter run

products.name: Gritin 10.2 Inch Motion Sensor Under Cabinet Light, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Gritin is aimed at people who care about the quality of the light, not just whether it turns on. Each 10.2 inch bar holds 84 LEDs, the highest count in this lineup, which gives an even strip of light without visible dots. The body is aluminum alloy with ABS plastic, a sturdier build than all-plastic bars.

Three color temperatures let you pick warm 3000K for a cozy kitchen at night or cool 6000K for task lighting, and five brightness levels cover everything in between. Four working modes include Off and Night Sensing, so you can decide whether the light runs on motion alone or only in the dark. That range is useful in a kitchen where the same bar does evening ambiance and morning prep.

More settings mean more to learn, and the listing does not state a battery capacity, so we cannot compare run time with the EZVALO's 2400mAh. The cool 6000K setting is too stark for a bedroom. Choose it when the quality of light is the priority. Keep the charging cable near the cabinet so a quick top-up never feels like a project.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want even, adjustable task lighting.
cons: Cool white is stark at night

products.name: YLXS 5-Pack Motion Sensor Under Cabinet Lights, 7.9 Inch
products.description:
The YLXS is the set to buy when you have several small spaces, such as a row of narrow cabinets or a pantry with multiple shelves. Five 7.9 inch bars come in one pack, each with 42 LEDs and a listed output of up to 100 lumens, which is the only brightness figure given among these picks. That makes it easy to judge how much light you are getting.

Three color temperatures and adjustable brightness let you match each space, and a built-in 1100mAh battery charges over USB-C. There are three work modes, including a Night Mode that lights on motion only in the dark. The compact size slips under shallow cabinets where a longer bar would not fit.

The 1100mAh battery is the smallest here, about half the size of the EZVALO's 2400mAh, so expect more frequent charging. Five batteries to recharge also adds up. Choose it for coverage of many small spaces. Label each bar with a marker so you know which is which when you take them down to charge.
products.bestFor: Pantries, narrow cabinets and shelves that need several short bars.

products.name: Auxoda 6-Pack Rechargeable Motion Under Cabinet Lights

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Always on, day, night and off

products.description:
The Auxoda is the pick when you want lots of lights for a large kitchen or several closets. Six lights come in the pack, each with a 2000mAh battery that the listing says lasts 30 to 60 days in sensor mode. The sensor covers 10 feet at 120 degrees, a respectable reach for a cabinet light.

It has four modes, always on, day mode, night mode and off. Day mode activates when motion is detected, and night mode does so only in the dark, which is a useful split between a pantry that you open in daylight and a counter you use at night. The lights fade up gradually, which feels gentler than an abrupt switch-on.

Six lights mean six batteries to maintain, though the 30 to 60 day range is a solid showing. The listing does not give an LED count, so brightness is hard to compare. Choose it when coverage matters more than a premium build. It also works well as a spare set to rotate in while the first lights are charging.
products.bestFor: Large kitchens or multiple closets that need many lights.
cons: Brightness is hard to judge from the listing

products.name: ASOKO 12 Inch Motion Sensor Cabinet Lighting, 3 Pack
products.description:
The ASOKO is a more traditional under cabinet bar that happens to have a motion sensor. At 12 inches it is the longest bar in the lineup, and the three-pack can be linked together, so a run of bars acts like one longer fixture. The 4500K daylight color is neutral and good for task lighting.

A built-in passive motion sensor works with an auto-off timer, so the light goes off once motion stops. Dimming is stepless from 0 to 100 percent through a three-button switch, and it remembers your last setting. There are three ways to install it, using strong magnetic clips or 3M stickers, with no electrician needed.

The listing does not state whether it is rechargeable or powered another way, so check how it is powered before buying. The 4500K tone is less warm than the 3000K options. Choose it for working counters where neutral light helps. Pair it with warmer bars elsewhere only if you do not mind two different tones in one room.
products.bestFor: Work counters that need neutral task lighting and linkable bars.
pros: 12 inch bars are the longest here
cons: Power source is not clearly stated

products.name: MCGOR 14.7 Inch Rechargeable Motion Under Cabinet Lights, 2 Pack
products.description:
The MCGOR is the longest rechargeable bar in the lineup at 14.7 inches, with 63 LEDs per bar. That length helps on deep shelves and wide counters where a short bar leaves dim corners. The frosted cover is meant to be non-glare, so the LEDs do not look like a row of bright dots.

It can run on motion sensing or be set to always-on, which is helpful when you are sorting items and do not want the light to switch off. Brightness is dimmable, and the bars attach magnetically, so installation takes seconds. Compared with the Gritin's 84 LEDs on a 10.2 inch bar, the MCGOR spreads fewer LEDs over a longer bar.

The listing gives no battery capacity, so run time is unclear. Two bars suit one long counter but not a whole kitchen. Choose it when length is the priority. Choose the always-on setting for sorting jobs and motion for everyday use.
products.bestFor: Deep shelves and long counters that need a longer bar.
cons: Fewer LEDs per inch than the Gritin

buyingCriteria.explanation: Wireless bars live and die by their battery. The EZVALO carries 2400mAh, the Auxoda 2000mAh and the YLXS 1100mAh. A bigger cell means fewer charges, which matters when the light triggers often. In a busy kitchen a bar will drain much faster than in a closet, so size the battery to the traffic.

Measure the underside of the cabinet before you buy. The YLXS bars are 7.9 inches, the EZVALO 10, the ASOKO 12 and the MCGOR 14.7. A bar that is too long will not fit a shallow cabinet, while one that is too short leaves dark corners. Allow a little space at each end for the magnet or adhesive.

Warm light feels cozy and cool light is better for tasks. The Gritin offers 3000K to 6000K, the YLXS offers three color temperatures and the ASOKO is 4500K daylight. A high color rendering makes food look natural, though listings rarely state it. Choose a warm setting for evening use and a neutral one for chopping.

The sensor behavior decides when the light helps. The EZVALO has a Night Motion Mode, the Auxoda has day and night modes, and the Gritin has Night Sensing. A mode that works only in the dark saves charge during the day. Always-on mode is useful when you are working at the counter for a while.

Most bars attach with magnets or adhesive. The ASOKO offers magnetic clips and 3M stickers, and the MCGOR is magnetic. A magnet needs a metal surface or a plate under the cabinet, and adhesive needs a clean, dry underside. Check what you are fixing to before you order.

A pack of two covers one counter, while the YLXS gives five and the Auxoda six. More bars mean more batteries to charge and more spaces lit. Count the spaces first. A few well-placed bars usually beat many scattered ones.

faq.q: How do I choose the right bar length?
faq.a: Measure the underside of your cabinet and subtract an inch or two for the mount. Bars here run from 7.9 inches on the YLXS to 14.7 inches on the MCGOR. A longer bar lights more of the counter, while a shorter one fits tight spaces and shallow cabinets.

faq.q: Do wireless under cabinet lights need wiring?
faq.a: No. The rechargeable bars attach with magnets or adhesive and charge over a cable, which makes them suitable for rented homes. Check the ASOKO listing for how it is powered, since it does not say clearly. No electrician is needed for any of the picks here.

faq.q: How long will the battery last?
faq.a: The Auxoda lists 30 to 60 days in sensor mode. Other listings give no run time, so use the milliamp-hour rating as a guide, with 2400mAh on the EZVALO well above the 1100mAh on the YLXS. A busy kitchen will drain a bar faster than a closet.

faq.q: Which color temperature should I choose?
faq.a: Warm 3000K feels cozy for evenings, while 4500K to 6000K is better for tasks such as chopping. Several bars here offer three options so you can switch. Choose warm for night use so you keep your night vision.

faq.q: Can the lights stay on all the time?
faq.a: Some can. The MCGOR and Auxoda offer always-on modes, and the Gritin includes several working modes. Always-on drains the battery much faster, so reserve it for jobs where you need steady light.

faq.q: Will the sensor see me from across the kitchen?
faq.a: The Auxoda lists 10 feet at 120 degrees. Other listings give no range, so test the placement before you stick anything down. Aim the sensor along your usual path to the counter.

faq.q: Can I use these in a closet instead?
faq.a: Yes, they are commonly used that way. A short bar like the YLXS fits closet shelves well. Make sure the magnet or adhesive suits the surface, and keep the sensor facing the door.
